name: Electrocyte Organ Array
description: Introduces electric eel electrocyte cells into modified muscle tissue in the forearms and hands, creating a biological capacitor that can discharge up to 400 volts in a brief, directed pulse through skin contact. The organ charges passively from metabolic processes and requires approximately 15 minutes between full discharges. Partial discharges are possible — a warning shock of 50 volts or a sustained low-voltage current for powering small electronics. Crucible Genomics' premium installation includes forearm electrocyte arrays large enough for ranged discharge across a 2–3 centimeter air gap. The user's own nervous system is insulated through modified myelin sheaths. The modification is visibly identifiable — forearms are slightly thicker than normal, and the skin over the electrocyte arrays has a faintly ridged texture. During charging, some users report a crackling sensation.
procedure: Forearm muscular augmentation surgery with retroviral electrocyte induction, 3 sessions over 4 weeks
expression_time: 8–12 weeks for full organ development; discharge capacity increases over 6 months
reversibility: Surgically removable; forearm musculature may be permanently altered
side_effects: Involuntary discharge during sleep or startle response
Electronic devices malfunction near the user during high charge states
Forearm muscle cramps during rapid recharging
Metallic taste in mouth when fully charged
Rare: cardiac arrhythmia from internal current leakage
social_perception: Respected and feared in equal measure. Livewire users are treated like people who carry visible weapons — given space in crowds, treated carefully in negotiations. The modification is popular among bodyguards, enforcers, and people who live in dangerous neighborhoods.
story_hooks: A Livewire user discovers their discharge has been gradually increasing beyond safe parameters — the electrocyte organs are growing, and nobody knows why
An EMP weapon designed to disable cyberware also triggers involuntary discharge in every Livewire user in the area, causing a chain reaction of electrical injuries
